title: Forbidden Siren 2
subtitle: An island whose past will not stay buried
summary: Forbidden Siren 2 is Sony's PlayStation 2 survival-horror game, first released in Japan on 9 February 2006. Several people become trapped on Yamijima Island, where the population vanished during a blackout decades earlier. A capsized ferry and a crashed military helicopter bring different characters into the same mystery. The story is experienced out of order, letting one person's discoveries change the meaning of another's predicament. Its island becomes a place the player learns through overlapping fragments, while the immediate problem remains finding a way past the hostile figures moving through the dark.
body: Forbidden Siren 2 is Sony's PlayStation 2 survival-horror game, first released in Japan on 9 February 2006. Several people become trapped on Yamijima Island, where the population vanished during a blackout decades earlier. A capsized ferry and a crashed military helicopter bring different characters into the same mystery. The story is experienced out of order, letting one person's discoveries change the meaning of another's predicament. Its island becomes a place the player learns through overlapping fragments, while the immediate problem remains finding a way past the hostile figures moving through the dark.

Sightjacking allows the player to look through the perceptions of other characters and enemies, gathering information that the protagonist cannot safely obtain in person. That borrowed view can reveal a patrol's position or a route that might otherwise be approached blindly. Missions ask for specific objectives, often involving escape, an item or an enemy that must be dealt with. The Link Navigator organises the scenarios and their relationships. An action in one part of the story can make another objective possible elsewhere, turning the chronology into part of the puzzle.

Keiichiro Toyama directed the sequel, with Naoko Sato contributing to the writing and Kuniaki Haishima composing its music. The cast's intersecting stories and unusual ways of seeing continue the first Siren's approach to survival horror. Japanese, Australian and European releases arrived in 2006, but the game did not receive a North American edition. Its fear grows from imperfect information: the player can borrow another viewpoint without gaining complete control of the situation. Understanding what an enemy sees is useful precisely because being seen by that enemy can be disastrous.

See the danger from another pair of eyes
Another strand of Sony's horror games
